Can the minister say what buildings the expenditure was made on, where they are located, and how much was spent on each?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works
speechtext: I shall be glad to send my hon. friend the full details.
Nearly twenty years ago a branch of the Public Works Department was established in the town of North Sydney. We had three or four engineers and quite a staff; the men had their homes there-

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works
speechtext: If my hon. friend will permit me to interrupt, I would point out that on page 44 of the Estimates there is an item with regard to the engineering services. I intimated to the committee on Wednesday evening that I had a statement to make with regard to the engineering services, and if my hon. friend will defer his question until that time, I shall be glad to answer any questions that may be asked. Of course, I am prepared to answer him this evening if he wishes, but the matter could more appropriately be discussed then.

Perhaps the minister will permit me to finish; I was in the middle of a sentence. My complaint is
that he has treated North Sydney in a very unkindly way, and when he gets to that other item I shall discuss the matter further. There was no justification for taking this institution away from our town except the desire on the part of the minister to take everything to Halifax. We had the headquarters of the one steamer belonging to the Public Works Department at North Sydney-the proper place for a steamer doing work along that coast, but the steamer had to be taken away too. I say now that when the proper item is under consideration I shall lodge my complaint at the door of the department, and particularly of the minister, for taking away that part of our population and all that it meant to us. The people of North Sydney will remember the Tory Government and the Department of Public Works and all the paraphernalia of this Admin-tration when they are asked to express an opinion regarding the Government's conduct.

I desire to draw the minister's attention to a case which I think is already engaging the mind of the department. I refer to the post office at Clark's Harbour, Shelburne county. Clark's Harbour is now an incorporated town, and with the natural ambition of a young, progressive community they have sent in an application for a new public building. I quite concur in the view that large public buildings of an expensive character cannot be undertaken at present, but the need for at least a temporary accommodation in this case is very great. I simply desire to urge the importance of having something done in this respect as soon as possible.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works
speechtext:
Representations have
come to the department, initiated by the postmaster at Clark's Harbour, who, I believe, sent word that the offices which for years had been used as a post office there would no longer be available. Speaking from memory, I believe that a proposal was made by the postmaster that other accommodations of a very satisfactory nature could be obtained, but later advices were received from him that his expectations in that regard had failed of fulfilment. But the department is still looking for improved premises at Clark's Harbour. I quite appreciate the point put forward by my hon. friend and I assure him that the very natural desires of the people of Clark's Harbour will have most sympathetic consideration.

With
reference to the point raised by the hon. member for Cape Breton, I would like to ask the minister what has been done with regard to the reorganization of the Public Works Department in Nova Scotia, and how it atfects the office in Antigonish? The committee has not had any statement as to what policy the minister has adopted in regard to the changes made.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works
speechtext:
As I intimated to the hon. member for North Cape Breton, I have a statement to make in regard to engineering services when item No. 154 comes up for consideration. I shall then have much pleasure in covering my hon. friend's question.
Saskatchewan-Public buildings, $20,000.

I do not complain about the minister not spending money, but I would like to ask how it comes that Saskatchewan, a province with a population the third largest in the Dominion, has a vote of $20,000 for public buildings while Nova Scotia has a vote of $207,000, and other provinces in proportion?

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works
speechtext: We are simply asking Parliament to give us the vote reported by our officials in Saskatchewan as being necessary to take care of casual matters coming up in connection with the public buildings.

In the interest of
economy, it might be a good move for the minister to send his Saskatchewan officials down to Nova Scotia or some of the other provinces for a year or two.

speechtext: Item agreed to.

speakerposition: Minister of Public Works
speechtext:
We had a long sitting last night, and we have had an expeditious sitting to-night, having put a good deal of business through. I therefore move that the committee rise, report progress and ask leave to sit again.
Progress reported.
